body:
Path strings outside of external resource tags should generally not happen. The code that creates this metadata was added in #86781.

So safe to say its not a regression at least

I also stumbled over this.
- Create a script with a `class_name`
- create scene
- add a node of that class
- save the scene
- rename the script file **outside** of the editor
- reload project
- open the scene
- fix the dependency by selecting the new script location
- open the scene
- select the node
- \*crash\*

I know that the rename step is not the regular way to work with Godot, but neither a crash.

The project after fixing the dependency

[new_game_project.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/18917033/new_game_project.zip)

Trying to get a stacktrace but failing due to lack of debug symbols in official builds

In 4.4rc3, I can reproduce the crash by selecting node3d and back to the class_name node a few times.
I cannot reproduce the build on a MSVC build of master (15ff4506) with debug symbols.

I don't know if the issue is MSVC or if some patch snuck in after RC3 that fixed this, or it's nondeterministic in a weird way.

I have made 4 attempts to follow @IceflowRE 's steps on both my MSVC build and on official 4.4rc3, and crashes 100% of the time on official build, and never crashes on MSVC.

@lyuma Official builds are made with mingw-gcc ([versions here](https://github.com/godotengine/build-containers?tab=readme-ov-file#toolchains)) and `lto=full`, both of which may have an impact if there's a compiler specific issue.

I tested with official 4.4.rc3 on Linux (also built with GCC, but not for Windows) and can't reproduce the crash.

Probably fixed by [#103467](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/103467)

I follow @IceflowRE steps at Linux.
